name: Commonborn
summary: The body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a Commonborn must settle on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. Mind is closed to it outright — a body this even has no native faculty for it. (full text in lore/prose/races/commonborn.md)

name: Emberblood
summary: A body that runs hot and short. It refines qi faster than anything here and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, at the cost of a lifespan measured in decades rather than centuries and a mind path that closes once the furnace is lit. Fire affinity is structural, not a gift.

name: Emberborn
summary: A line from the founding generation of a body that burned through its own reserve and kept going. Recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception and have stayed crossed since, which is why the concentration is thin and unevenly spread. The grant is defensive and fires continuously: a slower burn rather than a bigger tank.

name: Hearthborn
summary: The default concentration found in long-settled households: a lineage carried carefully for many generations, averaged with whatever else the household took in. Common as a stat-block and unsurprising as a reading — most actors hold some, and most never cross its bar. Its grant is small on purpose; the line is common because it is dependable, not because it is strong.

name: Stoneborn
summary: A dense, slow body assembled for load-bearing work. It carries more physique and stamina than anything else here and it stops at the Immortal tier, because the density that makes it durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form. Mind cultivation is closed outright.

name: Tideborn
summary: The oldest recorded carrier line, kept in one household so long that the name stopped describing a family and started describing a body. Two generations of pure pairing is the most this line has ever held, and the bar is set where it is because that is exactly the ceiling of an unbroken chain. Its grant trades immediate impact for sustained pressure: nothing here lands harder, everything here lasts.

name: Tidecaller
summary: A long-lived body built for perception rather than force. Comprehension and will carry it through realms that would end a hotter body, and it cannot take the body path at all: it was assembled for looking, not for being hit. Water affinity is the only one it holds.

name: Tideculled
summary: A line maintained by a clan that culled its own branches rather than marrying out of them. The concentration survives because the gene pool was narrowed, not improved, and it crosses races freely — the cull was a political act, never an anatomical one. Its grant favours sustained effort over sudden effort: regen and cultivation pace, nothing that spikes.

name: Voidborn
summary: A line with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it. The founding bar is set at 0.72 because the arithmetic leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it: anything weaker is unobtainable by any pairing and the content would be dead. This lineage is the system's proof that its own ladder is reachable.

name: Saltfolk
summary: A people built for brine no softer body could drink. Their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which lets them live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back. The price is total dependence: a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying, and no cultivation repairs it. They exist because the brine does, which makes them a species of a resource rather than a nation of it.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:osmoregulation as a metabolic cost paid in time
abstract-pattern:desert peoples bound to a single aquifer

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 11 is the first gate demanding all four extraordinary vessels closed at once. The saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined. They clear the du and ren vessels one at a time and stall on the chong.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete; slower than a specialist because the same effort is spent on osmoregulation
cultivation_paths.body: complete, and a salt-dense frame resists what would break a Commonborn
cultivation_paths.mind: open, though salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air

attributes.origin: Evolved on dry interiors where surface water is more concentrated than blood. Every later decision is downstream of that one fact.
attributes.anatomy: Extraordinary renal mass, a brine sac dorsal to the sternum, a hardened dermal salt crust, and broad splayed feet for cracked pan. Teeth are flat for grinding crust, not sharp for tearing.
attributes.senses: Taste carries the species. They read brine concentration across four orders of dilution; to a human nose a saltfolk smells sour. Vision is no better than a Commonborn's and poor in glare.
attributes.diet: Halophilic algae, mineral crust, and protein soaked past saturation. With nothing else alive on the pan, they are its apex consumer.
attributes.reproduction: The zygote carries a brine load from conception and needs saturated welfare fluid; a dry birth kills the infant. Crosses Commonborn readily and yields plain saltfolk, which is why they turn up far from any pan.
attributes.weaknesses: Cannot drink fresh water and fails above the brine line within about nine days. Rain is a hazard, not a blessing: a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning.
attributes.soul_meridian: A normal qi-bearing soul, seated high in the chest to keep it clear of the brine sac. The reservoir channels are the structural defect that sets their ceiling.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world dry interior: salt pans, wadi floors, evaporite basins. Needs a standing brine supply within a day of travel, which is why they are the least mobile people here.
attributes.soul_after_death: The soul releases cleanly and is recoverable. Saltfolk burial is a practical matter, not a sacred one, because a recovered soul is reusable.

name: Marshfolk
summary: A wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a Tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between. The three-point stance that lets them move through silt never loads a heel, which is why they cannot form the two heel vessels and stop at the fourteenth gate. They exist to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:amphibian re-entry as a stable third niche

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 14 is the first gate that requires both heel vessels simultaneously. The marshfolk wading frame is a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, so the heel never takes a full load and qi never pools there. They walk fine. They cannot stand still.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and quick in wet qi, markedly slower on dry land
cultivation_paths.body: complete, but soft-tissue and low against mineral bodies
cultivation_paths.mind: open; a body used to reading silt and current is patient by default

attributes.origin: Evolved on floodplain margin, occupying the band neither dry-land nor open-water selection could take.
attributes.anatomy: Long legs with a splayed three-point foot, a prehensile tail-prop, feathered inlet/outlet, and a ventral brood pouch. No heel, and no structure in its place.
attributes.senses: Pressure through the feet and taste of silt carry the world to them. They feel a vibration through standing water long before they see its source.
attributes.diet: Silt algae, rootstock, waterfowl eggs, and anything that falls in. Deliberately broad, because the floodplain's menu is unreliable by nature.
attributes.reproduction: Eggs laid in a mat of woven reed, carried under the brood pouch through the dry season, and hatched when the water returns. Fertilisation is external and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is.
attributes.weaknesses: Skin desiccates fast out of water, so travel is timed to the flood. Long dry seasons kill the young first.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi pools low and wide in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, which is why they take qi out of wet ground efficiently and dry ground poorly.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world floodplain margin: reed beds, seasonal marsh, delta edge. Needs standing shallow water within an hour of where it sleeps.

name: Ashwalker
summary: A body that breathes volcanic grit and keeps it, built where airborne ash would destroy softer tissue in a season. The mineral load in their blood settles on the liver first, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so they stop at the eighth gate. The same grit occludes the fine vessels introspection needs, which is why the mind path is closed to them outright.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:heavy-metal burden as a trophic strategy
abstract-pattern:particulate damage closing one cognitive niche

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: The eighth gate completes the ordinary meridian set at the liver. The ashwalker carries a suspended mineral load in the blood that filters through the liver, and the liver is the first organ to fail under it. They stop one step short of the reservoirs because they cannot hold the last ordinary meridian.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and durable; qi is processed through the same filter as air
cultivation_paths.body: complete, and the frame is genuinely dense under load
cultivation_paths.mind: closed. Particulate grit occludes the fine capillary beds that introspection needs, and the species has no faculty left for it

attributes.origin: Evolved on the ash-fall belt of an active volcanic arc, where the air is a delivery mechanism for rock.
attributes.anatomy: A chambered nasal sieve lined with cilia that trap grit and pass it into a crop for grinding, a thickened dermis, and a dark mineral-charged blood. Enamel is grey and pitted from grit, not from diet.
attributes.senses: Smell is effectively gone, replaced by the sieve's direct contact sense. They taste minerals the way a Commonborn tastes salt, and are the only population that can tell two ash grades apart by tongue.
attributes.diet: Ash-scoured lichen, mineral precipitate, and sulfur-bearing roots. They process stone into protein and are the only reason the ash belt has a food chain at all.
attributes.reproduction: Internal, live, and slow to establish. A pair must be within sight of each other through the ember season or conception does not hold, which sets their whole social spacing.
attributes.weaknesses: Water scarcity and any airborne toxin their sieve does not recognise. A whiff of a soft poison is a wound; they have no second line.
attributes.soul_meridian: Strongly qi-bearing and unusually durable, seated low and heavy. The soul survives ordinary death intact but is hard to lift clear, which is why recovery rites for them are laborious.
attributes.environment: Mortal- and spirit-world volcanic belts, ash-fall fans, geothermal ground. Needs a persistent ash source; a quiet decade is a slow decline.

name: Lanternfolk
summary: A cave people who have outsourced their nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through their skin, which is why they are still alive at two hundred and fifty years and cannot take the mind path: there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. Their light is a waste product of a symbiosis they did not choose, and it is the only reason the deep caves have an economy at all.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:troglobitic loss of eyes and pigment
abstract-pattern:proxy sense through symbiotic response patterns

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: No ceiling. Their limit is not a gate but a ceiling of a different kind: the colony renews neural tissue faster than a human body does, so age stops mattering, and nothing in their structure refuses a realm. They are long-lived because they are being repaired, and the repair is not free.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and the best qi regeneration in the species record, because the colony transacts with the air
cultivation_paths.body: complete but slow, and comparatively fragile in a fight
cultivation_paths.mind: closed. The colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior to cultivate

attributes.origin: Evolved in lightless cave systems from a lineage that lost its eyes first and negotiated the colony second.
attributes.anatomy: A colony of fine luminous hyphae threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord. Human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ; neither can be removed from the other and survive.
attributes.senses: Chemoreception and vibration, both very good. Their light is useless to them — it is emitted, not received — and they read surfaces by the pattern of fungal response a hand makes on the wall.
attributes.diet: Fungal matter, mineral seepage, and the small amount of protein the colony can fix from cave air. They eat almost nothing by weight and are never hungry.
attributes.reproduction: A colony fragment is transferred to the infant during gestation and the pair must find a matching strain within the first year or the colony rejects the child. Fertility is low and the pairing ritual is long.
attributes.weaknesses: Cannot leave the cave system. Dry, sunlit, or vibrating ground kills the colony within a season, and the body goes with it. Fire is the one thing that ends them quickly.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and unusually fluid. Because the colony transacts with the surrounding qi directly, the meridian network is a highway rather than a pipeline — which is why there is no structural ceiling at all.
attributes.environment: Mortal- and spirit-world cave systems, deep karst, lava tubes. Needs saturated air, near-constant humidity and a compatible fungal strain within range.

name: Longwinter
summary: A cold-climate species that survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle, packing a winter as body fat rather than as qi. That single decision puts the flank vessels out of reach: they need two warm gradients held at once, and a longwinter only has one, briefly, in summer. They reach far and never stay there, which is why they are the setting's best long-haul traders.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:hibernation as a seasonal state machine

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 17 is the first gate requiring both flank vessels pressurised at once. A longwinter carries its winter as fat and lowers its core temperature for eleven months; the flank vessels need two warm gradients held simultaneously, which this body can manage for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. They reach the seventeenth gate and lose it every winter thereafter.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and slow; the same cycle that stores fat stores qi
cultivation_paths.body: complete and excellent, and better for it after a hibernation
cultivation_paths.mind: open; the species is patient by physiology rather than by discipline

attributes.origin: Evolved on a high-latitude steppe where the growing season is short enough that survival is a storage problem.
attributes.anatomy: Broad low frame, heavy subcutaneous fat, a lowered cold-tolerant core, and reduced limb length. Warm-blooded but not expensive to run.
attributes.senses: Smell is their navigation system; they have tracked a fixed route over open ground for generations. Hearing is good. Vision is mediocre and they rely on scent markers, which they leave deliberately.
attributes.diet: Almost anything, taken in enormous quantities during eleven weeks and stored. Their digestion extracts more from frozen food than any other body in the record.
attributes.reproduction: Conception is timed so that birth lands in the thaw and the infant's first hibernation is its second summer. A mis-timed conception is the single largest cause of longwinter infant loss.
attributes.weaknesses: Slow and nearly helpless during torpor. A hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target and cannot be woken quickly.
attributes.soul_meridian: The soul is held very deep and very quiet, which makes it difficult to read and exceptionally hard to damage. Qi accumulates rather than circulates, so their breakthroughs are late and rarely fail.
attributes.environment: Mortal- and spirit-world cold steppe, high latitude, alpine meadow. Needs a real winter. A warm year is a bad year; a warm decade is a catastrophe.

name: Ashjackal
summary: A pack quadruped that eats what qi leaves behind, born where the dead are the most reliable food and a predator that cannot take them is what survives. Their heat-exchange brainplate leaves no folding for a mind path to work on and no hindquarters to close a girdling vessel, so they are the fastest body on the ash and it is why.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:obligate scavenger guild as a stable trophic role
abstract-pattern:heat-exchange cranial plate as a thermal adaptation
abstract-pattern:quadruped load paths determining achievable gates

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Two independent walls, and neither is negotiable. The mind path is closed because a heat-exchange brainplate has no cortical folding for introspection to work on. The body path is closed because qi cannot be stored in a frame built to shed heat. They clear the twelve ordinary meridians and stop, because a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth with which to close the girdling vessel.

cultivation_paths.qi: the only open path, and it is fast; ashjackal absorb residual qi out of ash and carcass at a rate nothing else matches
cultivation_paths.body: closed. A frame built to shed heat cannot be built to store it
cultivation_paths.mind: closed. No cortical folding; the pack runs on scent-pheromone relay, not introspection

attributes.origin: Evolved on the ash belt as the obligate scavenger of a world where most deaths are violent and unattended.
attributes.anatomy: Long-legged, low-headed, with a plated skull that dissipates heat, a second stomach for fermentation, and a tail-counterbalance rather than a manipulator. The forelimbs carry all of the mass.
attributes.senses: Olfaction is a map. They read a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, and the pack relay carries it to each other within seconds.
attributes.diet: Carrion, ash, and residual qi out of spent ground. They are the only population that thrives where nothing was killed deliberately.
attributes.reproduction: Short gestation, large litters, and no pair bond. A pack is a kinship by scent and dissolves when the scent changes, which is why packs are not families.
attributes.weaknesses: Cannot take a healthy adult of anything. They eat the aftermath and are removed from a live fight in under a minute.
attributes.soul_meridian: Present, strong, and almost immobile. The qi network is a fast single loop with no storage at all, which is why their breakthroughs are early and terminal.
attributes.environment: Ash belts, dry battlefield margins, spent ground, and the leeward side of anything that kills in quantity. Follows carrion populations; does not precede them.

name: Cairnborn
summary: A body that finished building and stopped. Cairnborn were shaped for load-bearing masonry work in high country and their interiors mineralised into a single cavity, which is why the whole yin-organ gate is missing from them: there is no heart, no kidney, no paired structure to run qi between. Stoneborn are what you get breeding them back toward flesh, and they are more alive and less capable for it.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:cast-and-key construction as a reproductive mode
abstract-pattern:structural loss of serial organ pairing

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 5 is the first gate requiring the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. The cairnborn interior is one cavity: a slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular. There is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, and no bladder to hold. They clear the gate set and never reach the yin organs.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete as far as the gate set goes, then structurally stops
cultivation_paths.body: complete and extreme; a cairnborn is the densest body in the record and the least mobile
cultivation_paths.mind: closed. No cortex, no folding, and a tidal circulation that would drown an interior voice

attributes.origin: Shaped deliberately for load-bearing masonry in high country, then stabilised by mineral seeding until the shape held on its own.
attributes.anatomy: A mineral lattice with a tidal interior. No differentiated organs; one cavity, one slow circulation, and a set of anchor plates keyed to whatever it was cast around. It does not grow after casting.
attributes.senses: Vibration and load through the plates. Excellent at feeling a structure move, blind to anything that does not put weight through the frame.
attributes.diet: None. It takes in mineral slurry through the cast faces and expels the residue. It has not eaten in four hundred years and cannot be made to.
attributes.reproduction: Cast, not born. A cairnborn is produced by seeding a template with living mineral, which takes most of a year, and the resulting body is fixed from that moment. Fertility is a template count, not a body count.
attributes.weaknesses: Cannot move quickly, cannot learn, and cannot be repaired in the field. A cracked plate is permanent and spreads.
attributes.soul_meridian: A qi-bearing soul seated in the single cavity, enormous and slow. It is legible from outside, which is why a cairnborn can be sworn to and a cairn site can be claimed.
attributes.environment: Spirit- and immortal-world high country, walls, dams, load paths, and the foundations under them. Needs to be keyed into something that bears load; unkeyed, it settles and cracks.

name: Rootmarch
summary: A sap-driven body that flowers. Rootmarch were engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, and they pay for it with the yin-organ gate: sap columns branch but they do not pair, so a rootmarch has no heart-kidney channel and never gets past the fourth realm. They are the reason the tier records a plant life form at all.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:sap transport in woody plants as a qi substrate

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 5, the yin-organ gate, for a structural reason: sap columns branch but they do not pair. A rootmarch has no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, and the gate demands a channel running between distinct pairs of them. It has three columns and no pairing, so there is no channel to close. They clear the gate set on stored sap alone.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete to the gate set, and unusually efficient in soil qi
cultivation_paths.body: closed. There is no tissue to temper; wood is not muscle and cannot be made to be
cultivation_paths.mind: open; a plant lineage has no reason to be hurried

attributes.origin: Engineered upward from a mycorrhizal food crop by generations of selection for harvest holding rather than yield.
attributes.anatomy: A woody column body on a root foot, with three sap columns and no organ pairs. Photosynthetic flanks, a fruiting shoulder, and no mouth in the ordinary sense — intake happens through root plates.
attributes.senses: Root-plate chemoreception and slow light sense across the photosynthetic flanks. Slow to react and impossible to surprise from above, because being surprised requires noticing.
attributes.diet: Photosynthesis, soil, and mineral water. A rootmarch can be sealed in a dark field and still live for months, which is a famine reserve and a hostage in equal measure.
attributes.reproduction: Seed. A fruiting shoulder sets, the fruit drops, and the seed takes root. Gestation is long and establishment is the dangerous part, not conception.
attributes.weaknesses: Fire, frost below a threshold, and being moved while rooting. A rootmarch lifted from its bed is a stored harvest walking, and it knows it.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and diffuse, held in the sap column rather than seated. It reads as a spread rather than a point, which makes it hard to target and easy to starve.
attributes.environment: Spirit- and immortal-world temperate ground, deep soil, shaded forest. Needs rooting depth and a growing season; it does not travel once rooted.

name: Cinderkin
summary: An elemental body, needing a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all. They are the reason the elemental law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on cold produces a different body entirely. They are also the thing that killed the Glasskin, which is the clearest evidence in the record that an element is a process and not an object.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:fire ecology and the limits of fuel and water
abstract-pattern:reproduction by fission under pressure rather than by birth

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: No ceiling, and no gate to fail. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in: the fire is the body, so qi passes through it continuously instead of being stored. Every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly, and none of them can refuse.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and the fastest qi handling in the record, because nothing is ever stored
cultivation_paths.body: closed. There is no tissue. A cinderkin that attempts the body path simply disperses and re-forms smaller
cultivation_paths.mind: open and unusually clear; a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air

attributes.origin: Not descended. Constituted where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something metabolises it.
attributes.anatomy: A stable flame with a consistent silhouette: a core, a boundary, and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape. It has no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense, and no fixed mass.
attributes.senses: It is a heat differential in a conversation with its surroundings. It reads temperature, fuel and flow directly, and has no other channel.
attributes.diet: Fuel and air. It will eat anything combustible, and it goes quiet rather than die when starved.
attributes.reproduction: None, and this is the point. A cinderkin does not have young; it has pressure. A cinderkin under enough stress sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate.
attributes.weaknesses: Water. Deep water. Not a splash — a sustained volume. It is also bound to its law slot: change what the slot resolves to and the population changes with it.
attributes.soul_meridian: The soul is the flame and it is genuinely qi-bearing, but it has no seat. A cinderkin's qi is entirely in transit, which is why nothing can be stored in one and nothing can be lost from one either.
attributes.environment: Immortal- and transcendent-world only, and only where the elemental law slot resolves to fire. A mortal world has three law slots and no room for an elemental body at all.

name: Carrionfolk
summary: A body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. Their conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so the reservoir gate at the eleventh realm is not blocked but meaningless: they have nowhere to put qi that is not moving. They are the setting's memory and its scavengers, which is why every graveyard and every battlefield ends up with the same people near it.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:scavenger guild specialised on energy remains
abstract-pattern:conduit physiology without a storage organ

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 11 is not blocked for carrionfolk, it is meaningless, and the difference matters. Their conduit has no dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow, and it is never still. The reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold. They clear the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and unmatched for throughput: they absorb residual qi from the dead at a rate nothing else approaches
cultivation_paths.body: complete, and useless — they cannot store power, so they win by never stopping
cultivation_paths.mind: open and good; the species reads a corpse's qi residue better than a living cultivator reads their own

attributes.origin: Evolved in the ecological shadow of every violent death on the ash belt, where a slow scavenger who can read qi out of a corpse eats better than a predator.
attributes.anatomy: An expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle. They are mostly tube. Hands are three-fingered and built for opening, not holding.
attributes.senses: They taste qi the way a Commonborn tastes salt. Given time with a body, they can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped.
attributes.diet: The dead, principally. Residual qi out of spent ground and discarded elixirs are supplements. Living food is possible and they find it unsatisfying.
attributes.reproduction: Very slow, very rare, and expensive. A carrionfolk conception is treated as an event rather than a routine, because the population is held up by the throughput of the dead, not by births.
attributes.weaknesses: A full gut is a near-total loss of function. Starves in a clean, quiet place where nothing dies, which is exactly what a prosperous city is.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and permanently in motion. The soul is legible and unusually old for its apparent age, and it does not disperse at death — it disperses into whatever killed it, which is where their reputation for reading the dead comes from.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world leeward ground: battlefield margins, execution ground, graveyard hinterland, spent qi fields. Follows death, so it is present everywhere there is a war and absent everywhere there is not.

name: Longmarrow
summary: The long-lived marrow-bodied race, and the reason the record's other longevity strategies exist at all. Their qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so they live four centuries and think in lengths no one else can hold. They cannot take the body path, because hardening the bone stops the turnover their qi depends on — the longest-lived body in the record is built out of the one material it may never stop replacing.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:bone-marrow as a renewable energy store
abstract-pattern:K-selected life history in a low-risk environment

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: No ceiling. Their qi is stored in bone marrow that turns over at roughly a percent a year, so there is no structural obstruction to any gate and no gate that has ever refused a Longmarrow. The limitation is entirely downstream of that success: turnover is slow, so everything they do is slow, and nothing they have ever built survived to be inherited intact.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and unbounded, but slow; they store rather than move, so their breakthroughs are certain and late
cultivation_paths.body: closed. Hardening bone marrow stops the turnover the qi depends on, and a body-cultivated Longmarrow suffocates on its own reserves within a decade
cultivation_paths.mind: complete and the best in the record; four centuries of one subject is a discipline in itself

attributes.origin: Evolved where bone is the only renewable store available, in a lineage that traded every other adaptation for lifespan.
attributes.anatomy: Long marrow, dense bone, minimal muscle, and a slow metabolism keyed to turnover. They are light, fragile to force, and extraordinarily difficult to exhaust.
attributes.senses: Everything is slow and everything is deep. Given four centuries a Longmarrow reaches an acuity of pattern that is not supernatural, only patiently arrived at.
attributes.diet: Anything, slowly. They eat little and can go without for most of a season without consequence.
attributes.reproduction: The bottleneck of the entire species. Four hundred days of gestation and fertility near a sixth of a Commonborn's, over a four-century life, means the population is essentially static and every individual is individually irreplaceable.
attributes.weaknesses: They cannot fight and they know it. In a violent world this is the whole of their risk, and it is why they are organised as knowledge and not as force.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and seated in the marrow, which makes it the deepest and hardest to disturb soul in the record. A Longmarrow soul has usually been in one body for a very long time.
attributes.environment: Mortal-, spirit- and immortal-world temperate upland and sheltered coast. Needs a stable, quiet, long-lived place; they are terrible at moving and terrible at fighting.

name: Vaultborn
summary: A population that was sealed inside an object and has been answering the object's resonance ever since. Their qi comes from that one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one. Remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in this record is that completely non-portable.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:sealed artifact populations and localised adaptation

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 17 is the first gate needing two flank vessels pressurised at the same time. A vaultborn has exactly one pressure source — the resonance of the object it is sealed inside — and one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other, never both. They clear the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and lose at the flanks, not because the vessels are hard but because the supply is single.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and very strong inside the object, and collapses to nothing outside it
cultivation_paths.body: complete and slow; the frame is not what it is for
cultivation_paths.mind: open and exceptional, because a lifespan measured in the object's cycles is a long time to learn anything

attributes.origin: Not descended and not born. A population that was sealed inside an authored object and has been answering the object's resonance ever since.
attributes.anatomy: Unsettled and under-described. They are arranged along the object's inner surfaces, they take their shape from whatever they are standing on, and nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements.
attributes.senses: They hear the object. Every sound the object makes is legible to them as a position, and they navigate by it rather than by light.
attributes.diet: The object's resonance. They do not eat in any sense a person would recognise, and they are not observed to take anything.
attributes.reproduction: Uncertain and probably not reproductive at all. What looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a lot of faces.
attributes.weaknesses: Total dependence on a single object. There is no version of this species that survives being carried out of the seal, and no technique, item or realm that changes that.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and seated along the resonance path, which means a vaultborn's soul is distributed through the object rather than held in a body. Reading one is reading part of the object.
attributes.environment: A single authored containment, deep inland and high. There is no wilderness population and there never has been.

name: Wake
summary: A thing that is only entirely real while it is being misremembered, which is why it has no body, cannot cultivate, and copies itself out of other people's recollection instead of out of any parent. It exists on worlds whose life law has no slot to inscribe one, and the setting has a reason it fits nothing: it is not human, not beast and not spirit, because the world that could have chosen which of those it is never wrote the line.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:memory as a reproductive substrate in folklore

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: There is no ceiling because there is no ladder. A wake holds no qi of its own: every cultivation path is closed, and the only qi it ever wields is the qi of whoever is looking at it. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it is. It does not ascend; it is described.

cultivation_paths.qi: closed. A wake has no reservoir, no circulation and no interior; it borrows the qi of whoever is looking, and only for as long as they keep looking
cultivation_paths.body: closed, and for the wrong reason — it has no body to temper
cultivation_paths.mind: closed, and this is the one it is least able to understand; it is an object of memory rather than a thing that remembers

attributes.origin: Not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when the world's life law has no slot in which to write the form down.
attributes.anatomy: None that holds. A wake's outline is supplied by the observer: it is tall to someone who expects tall, bent to someone who remembers it bent, and absent to anyone who is not thinking about it.
attributes.senses: It has no senses. It has an observer, and it knows the observer completely, including everything the observer would rather it did not know.
attributes.diet: Other people's recollection. It does not eat; it is sustained by being wrong about, and it grows denser the more it is agreed upon.
attributes.reproduction: By recall. A sufficiently vivid account of a wake, repeated in the right company, produces another one. No wake has ever been observed to produce its own kind deliberately, and that is the most unsettling fact about them.
attributes.weaknesses: Silence and inattention. A room that stops talking about a wake loses it. This is why the practice of not discussing them at length exists everywhere they have ever been reported.
attributes.soul_meridian: This is the whole problem. A wake has what reads as a soul and no soul-shaped structure: no seat, no circulation, and no meridian at all. Every scan returns it as either nothing or as the observer.
attributes.environment: Worlds whose life law runs at or below the bottom of its authored range, where a life form was permitted but never written down. Nowhere else.
attributes.status_reason: Reported, never verified. Every account is second-hand by construction, which is why no record of a wake is a record of one.

name: Echoless
summary: Human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them: a species the world permitted without inscribing, which is why it cannot cultivate, cannot be scanned, and passes every tribulation as an unremarkable object. It belongs to no culture, and this is not modesty — an Echoless can hold any culture perfectly and none of them will keep one, because nothing about the body gives anyone a reason to.

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: No ceiling, because there is nothing on a ladder. All three paths are closed and there is no gate to fail: an echoless has no qi to store, no refinement to refine and no introspection to interrupt. It is on the ladder's floor because it is not on the ladder.

cultivation_paths.qi: closed, permanently and without partial exception
cultivation_paths.body: closed
cultivation_paths.mind: closed
cultivation_paths.tribulation: an Echoless is simply not tribulated. It is attended, and then it is over

attributes.origin: A life-form allowance granted at the floor of the law's range: the world permitted a human body and did not write the qi component into it.
attributes.anatomy: A Commonborn body. This is the entire finding and it is the reason the species is a problem rather than a curiosity.
attributes.senses: Ordinary, and indistinguishable in use. Every test that works on a Commonborn works on an Echoless.
attributes.diet: Ordinary. It eats, works, ages and dies on the standard human schedule.
attributes.reproduction: Ordinary, and fertile. An Echoless child is an Echoless child, which is how nobody noticed for as long as they did.
attributes.weaknesses: It cannot be warned. A warning means qi, tribulation, technique, poison or curse, and none of these touch it. It is also the only body in the record with nothing to cultivate, so it is the only one that cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique.
attributes.soul_meridian: There is no meridian, no dantian and no qi, and there is also no soul that any instrument in this setting can detect. Whether anything is present is not a question the available methods can answer.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world anywhere, and especially anywhere a life law has been allowed to sit low for a long time. It does not need a homeland and this is exactly the difficulty.

name: Unwritten
summary: A body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe, produced when a life law runs above its authored ceiling. Every gate it passes writes a new requirement into the body that the body cannot satisfy, which is why it reaches the twenty-ninth gate and no one has ever come back to describe the thirtieth. It is the setting's standing argument that the law table is a hard limit and not a suggestion.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:specification limits exceeded as a failure mode

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 29 is the last gate that can be half-satisfied. Each gate an Unwritten passes writes a fresh requirement into the body, and the body cannot satisfy it because its life law has no slot to hold it — so the accumulated contradiction finally exceeds what the frame will bear at the twentieth-ninth gate. The thirtieth resolves all of it at once. Nobody has returned to describe the result and this record does not speculate about it.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and faster than anything else recorded
cultivation_paths.body: complete; the frame keeps accepting requirements it cannot meet
cultivation_paths.mind: closed, and for the whole reason. It cannot tell that it is inconsistent, because observing its own state would be one more requirement it has no slot for

attributes.origin: A world whose life law runs above the authored ceiling of 1.0, inscribing a life form with no room left to write it.
attributes.anatomy: Described only from the outside, and only by witnesses who were also describing an event. It has been seen to have every organ the ladder requires and to be carrying more of each than the ladder defines.
attributes.senses: Unreliable. Every report of an Unwritten's perception agrees that it perceived everything, which is exactly what a body with no unspent capacity for interior would appear to do.
attributes.diet: Not recorded. The only reliable datum is that an Unwritten has been observed for the better part of a year.
attributes.reproduction: None observed. There is one, as far as anyone can tell, and it is the reason the law table is treated as a ceiling rather than a suggestion.
attributes.weaknesses: It does not have a stable weakness. It has an *inconsistency*, which is not the same thing and which behaves very differently in a fight.
attributes.soul_meridian: Present, enormous, and carrying more meridians than the ladder defines. The mind path is closed because it cannot perceive its own contradiction.
attributes.environment: A transcendent-world or high immortal-world site where the life law has been pushed past its authored range. It does not spread and it does not persist.
attributes.status_reason: Recorded as unknown rather than active, because the only source is a single witness account of a single event, and because the thirtieth gate is genuinely undescribed.

name: Thornline
summary: An obligate host parasite whose spore has to be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the free form exists only as a spore and the adult form exists only as half of someone else. It wraps the host's twelve-meridian set and cannot enter the reservoirs, which is why its ceiling is the liver gate, and why the commonborn population is simultaneously its habitat and the reason it is persecuted.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:obligate parasitism with a free-living spore stage
abstract-pattern:host metabolic tolerance as a stable infection

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and goes no further, so it stops at the eighth gate. It is not a shortage — the host supplies qi in abundance — but a routing problem: the tendril layer has no passage through the host's liver, which is the first organ large and dense enough to resist it. The colony has been observed on the far side of that organ and it stops there.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete on the host's throughput, and the host pays for it
cultivation_paths.body: inherited from the host, not its own; a thornline has no body to speak of
cultivation_paths.mind: closed in the colony's own right. It answers introspection for the host, so the host loses the mind path too — the only case in the record where a body's liability is inherited rather than authored

attributes.origin: A free-living spore that became obligate because the host body was a better nutrient than anything it could reach alone.
attributes.anatomy: A tendril layer threaded along the host's meridians with a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat. The host grows it and the host is changed by it.
attributes.senses: The host's senses, plus the colony's read on the host's qi as a separate channel the host has no access to.
attributes.diet: The host's refined qi, drawn continuously. It takes a small fraction and the host does not lose weight, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that it is not simply a disease.
attributes.reproduction: Spore, shed at the fruiting node and implanted directly. It is common, contagious and almost impossible to acquire deliberately, which is precisely why every attempt has failed.
attributes.weaknesses: Total dependence. Killing the host kills the colony within the hour, and this is the reason thornline-host pairs are treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it.
attributes.soul_meridian: Two souls in one meridian set, which is the whole medical and legal problem. The colony's soul is legible but entangled, and separating them is known to be lethal to both.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world anywhere a commonborn population is dense enough to sustain it. It has no homeland because its habitat is a species.

name: Glasskin
summary: A human lineage whose members vitrified at maturity: a body that stopped ageing because it stopped being tissue. They were effectively immortal, completely defenseless against qi, and entirely unable to cultivate, and when a world's physical law was retuned to raise material hardness every existing body failed at once. No glasskin has been born since. Their record is the strongest available argument that a body is not a container for a person.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:mineral replacement of tissue as a freeze
abstract-pattern:immunity without agency as a trap
abstract-pattern:sudden law-change extinction of a whole clade

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 1, the floor, and there is no gate involved. A vitrified body has no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, because glass is not a conduit. It also has no qi to lose, which is why it is impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass.

cultivation_paths.qi: closed. Glass does not conduct
cultivation_paths.body: closed. There is nothing left in the body to temper
cultivation_paths.mind: closed. The tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue that was replaced

attributes.origin: A commonborn lineage under sustained selection toward stillness — an attempt to make a body that does not decay, which is the same mistake as asking a body not to age.
attributes.anatomy: Human to the last soft structure, then a progressive silicate replacement from the extremities inward. At full maturity: a standing glass cast in human proportions, with qi residue and a soul that scans as present and inert.
attributes.senses: None after vitrification, and the individual does not appear to want them. Nobody has ever reported a glasskin in distress and nobody has ever been able to ask one.
attributes.diet: None. Vitrification precedes the cessation of appetite, and the cast does not rot because it is not organic.
attributes.reproduction: Nearly none. Fertility fell to a twentieth of a Commonborn's over the lineage, and each generation vitrified later than the last, until the last cohort vitrified before it could breed and the line closed.
attributes.weaknesses: Everything that breaks glass, and nothing that fights qi. They were the most durable bodies in the record and the least capable of being harmed by anyone who understood what a meridian was.
attributes.soul_meridian: The soul is present, inert, and reads as sitting in a body. This is the reason the clade's destruction is a documented moral problem and not simply a solved question.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world cold, dry, mineral-rich highlands — the only places the silicate replacement could proceed without the body rejecting it. The last cohort was on one mountain.

name: Saltwrack
summary: A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so that everything it was built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted. There is nothing here of the usual kind of extinction: one element moved, and a species that had no alternative to that one element had nothing left.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:single-resource dependency as an extinction mechanism
abstract-pattern:gradual resource substitution rather than loss

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 11, the same wall every saltfolk has: the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel. They are recorded here because the wall was never what mattered. They never reached it, because they never got past the third generation of a famine.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and never exercised at any scale
cultivation_paths.body: complete and never exercised at any scale
cultivation_paths.mind: open and never exercised at any scale

attributes.origin: An offshoot of the saltfolk on a single evaporite basin whose brine was wholly replaced.
attributes.anatomy: A saltfolk body, slightly more gracile, with a shallower brine sac. The gracility is consistent across every specimen and is thought to be a real population difference rather than an artefact of the remains.
attributes.senses: Saltfolk senses throughout. Their taste could read the new brine perfectly well, which is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time.
attributes.diet: The basin's brine, and then nothing on it that would do. The replacement water was potable and was poison to them; the replacement crust was food and was nutritionally empty.
attributes.reproduction: It failed on schedule rather than all at once. Three declining generations, with the last one viable only as long as the old brine persisted in one sealed sump.
attributes.weaknesses: They had exactly one weakness and it was total. The species was defined by a single element, and the basin changed the concentration of that element rather than removing it.
attributes.soul_meridian: Saltfolk soul and meridian structure, without exception. Nothing about the clade's collapse left an anatomical trace, which is the reason it went unnoticed for two generations.
attributes.environment: One evaporite basin. There has never been any other, and there will not be another.

name: Deepsalt
summary: The saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent body until the brine is no longer a habitat but a requirement: a deepsalt taken above the brine line does not become ill, it simply stops. It is the clearest case in the record of a subspecies existing because a parent species was pushed further than it could carry.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:ecotype speciation along a single environmental gradient
abstract-pattern:obligate extremophily as a derived state

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 11, the same wall as the parent saltfolk: the brine sac runs dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it. The deeper sac is a larger obstruction, and they have simply never been tested at the reservoirs.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and faster than the parent body; saturated brine carries qi more readily than diluted
cultivation_paths.body: complete and the hardest frame in the species record
cultivation_paths.mind: open, and narrowly, with the same salt-head limitation

attributes.origin: Saltfolk pushed onto the saturated floor of a basin whose brine layer is thick enough to support a body in it permanently.
attributes.anatomy: A deeper, more capacious brine sac; a denser dermal crust; slower tissue turnover. Everything is the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down.
attributes.senses: Saltfolk senses with a far narrower usable range — they read concentration, not identity, and cannot tell two salts apart.
attributes.diet: Basin-floor precipitate only. They cannot use the pan organisms their parent eats.
attributes.reproduction: Slower than the parent and with a harder establishment period. A deepsalt infant is viable but brittle until the second year.
attributes.weaknesses: Total, and stricter than the parent: brine is not a preference but a substrate. Above the line they stop within hours.
attributes.soul_meridian: Saltfolk soul, seated a little lower because the sac is larger. Legible and durable.
attributes.environment: The saturated floor of one evaporite basin. There is no second population and there is not going to be one.

name: Deadlight
summary: Lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost them the two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path. It is the control case: everything the colony did for them and everything it prevented, recorded on a body where both can be measured against the parent species.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:symbiont replacement as a natural experiment

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: No ceiling. The mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and structurally unconstrained by it. What the subspecies gained is the mind path; what it lost is three quarters of its life.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete, and slower than the parent; a bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it
cultivation_paths.body: complete; the parent found this path slow and for the same reason
cultivation_paths.mind: open, and this is the entire point. Nothing answers introspection for them any more

attributes.origin: A lanternfolk lineage whose colony strain failed and which was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions.
attributes.anatomy: A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice in place of the hyphal colony. Lighter, colder, and entirely inert. The body grew around what replaced the fungus rather than recovering.
attributes.senses: Ordinary human vision. They see in the dark, unlike the parent, which is the single most-cited difference and the reason the subspecies is named for it.
attributes.diet: Ordinary, and far more than a lanternfolk eats. The bloom fixes nothing from the air.
attributes.reproduction: Ordinary human fertility and ordinary human gestation, which is roughly four times the parent's rate. They are the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them.
attributes.weaknesses: They live ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty, they are fragile, and they cannot leave the caves for exactly the reason the parent cannot. The shorter life is authored: a bloom renews nothing, so nothing in this body is being repaired.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing, seated in the body rather than answered by a colony. The mind path being open is direct evidence that the parent species' closed path was caused by the symbiosis and not by the body plan.
attributes.environment: The same cave systems as the parent lanternfolk. Neither can leave; only one of them can see.

name: Stonebound
summary: The documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, and the reason the Emberborn line is recorded alongside the stone line at all: they were crossed at one conception and have stayed crossed since. It is the most durable body anyone can build and it dies in about sixty years, and both facts are the same fact.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:stable interspecific hybrids as named lineages

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 4, the yin-organ gate, inherited from the mineral parent. The fire parent supplies heat and a mineral frame conducts it, so the tidal interior has a working circulation but no paired organ set to run a channel between. The heat does not help: a channel needs two organs and the stone body has one cavity.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and fast while the frame holds; the fastest qi throughput of any durable body
cultivation_paths.body: complete, and it is the entire point: the most durable body anyone can build
cultivation_paths.mind: closed, inherited from the mineral parent. A stonebound could take the mind path twice over and would not notice the difference

attributes.origin: A single recorded crossing of the mineral body with the fire body. It is documented because the resulting line was kept and named, not because the crossing was notable.
attributes.anatomy: A mineral lattice carrying a genuine fire circulation instead of a tidal one. Hot to the touch, denser than either parent, and visibly a compromise: the organ pairs are still not there.
attributes.senses: Load and heat. They feel a structure about to fail before it does, and they feel nothing at all through the mineral half.
attributes.diet: Anything the fire half can reduce. They eat constantly and burn it off immediately, which is why the mineral frame outlasts the fire parent's lifespan by a factor of two.
attributes.reproduction: Rare and deliberate. The Emberborn line exists because this crossing is stable enough to keep; the concentration is thin because it is one crossing and not a population.
attributes.weaknesses: The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished. A stonebound killed properly stays dead, and one injured stays injured. Sixty years.
attributes.soul_meridian: Qi-bearing and seated high in the frame, and durable in a way neither parent's soul is. It survives the body's death more reliably than the body survives anything.
attributes.environment: Volcanic and high country — the only ground where the two halves are not fighting each other. A stoneborn body and a stonebound body in the same climate is a comparison worth making.

name: Brinecaller
summary: The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones. It exists because both parents are trapped by their own element — one cannot leave the pan, the other cannot leave the water — and the cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, and it is why the crossing spread.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:ecological hybridisation at a boundary zone
abstract-pattern:dual substrate generalism and its costs

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 11, inherited from the salt parent and unchanged by the water one. The brine sac is smaller in a brinecaller but it is still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split. The watered parent has no such obstruction, which is why the cross widened the species' range without raising its ceiling — and range is not power.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete; noticeably slower than either parent in their own medium, and this is the cross's actual cost
cultivation_paths.body: complete and slightly better than either parent
cultivation_paths.mind: open; the least salted water-adapted body in the record, which is the point

attributes.origin: A crossing between the salt-adapted people and the fully watered ones, somewhere with a shoreline, which is the only place both parents can be at once.
attributes.anatomy: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus: dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once.
attributes.senses: The best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, because it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance and it is always being lied to by one of them.
attributes.diet: Both. This is the whole organism. A brinecaller eats the pan and the tide and does not need to travel between them to do it.
attributes.reproduction: Crosses freely in both directions and never produces a stable parent type, because the tolerance is a tolerance and not a plan. Fertility is ordinary and variance is high.
attributes.weaknesses: Nowhere native. It needs a shoreline, and a shoreline is a contested piece of ground, which is the practical reason the cross spread along trade routes rather than across them.
attributes.soul_meridian: A blended soul and a blended meridian set — a saltfolk spine with a tidecaller's chest seat. Perfectly legible, and structurally neither parent.
attributes.environment: Shorelines, estuaries, delta margins and salt-works. Needs both chemistries within reach, which is why it is found on coasts and almost nowhere else.

name: Emberhollow
summary: The fire body crossed with the ash body, which buys a cultivation rate nothing else reaches and pays for it with lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun. Their ceiling is the eighth gate for the reason their ash parent cannot pass it, and their reputation for being the best and the shortest-lived cultivators in any record is a single fact rather than two.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:sibling hybrids from a shared border zone
abstract-pattern:metabolic cost outrunning a favourable adaptation

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 8, the liver gate, inherited from the ash parent and made worse. The fire parent adds a heavier mineral load to a blood that is already filtering stone, so the organ that fails under the burden fails sooner. The ash parent could not hold the last ordinary meridian; an emberhollow cannot hold it and burns out trying.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete and the fastest rate in the record by a margin nobody has explained
cultivation_paths.body: complete and effective while the lungs hold
cultivation_paths.mind: closed, inherited from the ash parent and reinforced by the scarring

attributes.origin: A crossing between the fire body and the ash body on the volcanic belt where both are already present. Nobody chose it; it is what a shared border produces.
attributes.anatomy: An emberblood frame carrying an ash sieve, and the two do not have a good relationship: the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster and scars faster.
attributes.senses: Fast and shallow. They read intent quickly and have almost no patience, both of which are the fire parent's and neither of which helps.
attributes.diet: Combustible mineral and sulfur-root. They eat what they can burn and burn it inside themselves, which is convenient on the belt and fatal anywhere else.
attributes.reproduction: Frequent, fast, and high-variance. An emberhollow line is not stable across generations and everybody involved knows it.
attributes.weaknesses: Their own cultivation rate. They scar themselves out in under fifty years at a rate no technique in the record slows, and every account of an emberhollow dead at forty-five contains the word 'fast'.
attributes.soul_meridian: Strongly qi-bearing and short-fuse: the meridian set is the ash parent's, loaded with the fire parent's throughput, and it burns through reserves rather than accumulating them.
attributes.environment: The volcanic belt, and only the belt. They are the fastest cultivator in the setting and they cannot be moved off a rock.

name: Thornhost
summary: The one configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pairing is treated as one legal person in any jurisdiction that has ruled on it. The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, so the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's, which is the whole legal problem stated as a number.

provenance.author: w1-races
basis: abstract-pattern:stable host-parasite integration as a distinct class

attributes.realm_ceiling_mechanism: Ordinal 8, and it is the colony's ceiling rather than the host's. A thornline wraps the twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the host's liver; because the hybrid's qi moves through the colony's tendril layer, the host's own capacity is irrelevant past that point. The host could have gone on. The hybrid cannot.

cultivation_paths.qi: complete to the eighth gate, on the host's throughput and the colony's routing
cultivation_paths.body: inherited from the host and offset by the colony's durability
cultivation_paths.mind: closed in the colony's own right. A thornhost is the case the Thornline record refers to when it says the liability is inherited rather than authored

attributes.origin: Not a designed cross. A commonborn host and a thornline colony that completed integration instead of killing each other, which happens rarely and by no one's intention.
attributes.anatomy: A host body with a fully integrated tendril layer, a sternum root cluster and a quiet throat node. Neither half is anatomically dominant and the boundary between them is visible only under instrumentation.
attributes.senses: The host's, plus a second channel carrying the colony's read on the host's qi — a channel the host has never been able to close and has stopped trying to.
attributes.diet: Ordinary food plus whatever the colony draws. Small, steady, and cheaper than an uncolonised body of the same size.
attributes.reproduction: Rare. The colony is only transmissible in the one window where it has a compatible host, and the hybrid is very nearly a terminus — most attempts end in one half winning.
attributes.weaknesses: Everything a thornline has, plus one: the colony's ceiling is now the host's ceiling, so a thornhost is a person who cannot ascend for a reason they did not choose and cannot give up without dying.
attributes.soul_meridian: Two entangled souls on one meridian set, held stable by integration. The host's soul is legible; the colony's reads as a second presence rather than as absent.
attributes.environment: Mortal-world anywhere a commonborn population is dense. It has no homeland, because its habitat is a species and its habitat is a person.
